{{Short description|Taiwanese biochemist (1927–2019)}}
{{family name hatnote|[[Luo (surname)|Lo]]|lang=Chinese}}
'''Lo Tung-bin''' ({{zh|t=羅銅壁|p=Luó Tóngbì|w=Lo T'ung-pi}}; 15 February 1927 – 13 May 2019), also known as '''T. B. Lo''', was a Taiwanese biochemist. A pioneer in the research on [[proteins]] in Taiwan, he was elected an academician of [[Academia Sinica]] in 1986. He served as Dean of the College of Sciences of [[National Taiwan University]] and Vice President of Academia Sinica (1993–1996).

== Biography ==
Lo was born on 15 February 1927<ref>{{cite book|script-title=zh:中国国民党百年人物全书|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NcQyAQAAIAAJ&q=LuoTongbi |year=2005|publisher=Tuanjie Publishing |isbn=9787802140394}}</ref> in [[Puli, Nantou]], [[Japanese Taiwan]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.mh.sinica.edu.tw/MHWeb/PGPublication_Detail.aspx?pubid=738&majorTypeCode=1&minorTypeCode=10|title=臺灣蛋白質化學研究的先行者──羅銅壁院士一生回顧|last=Lo|first=Tung-bin|date=January 2016|publisher=Institute of Modern History, Academia Sinica|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-05-27}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite book|script-title=zh:臺灣蛋白質化學研究的先行者 : 羅銅壁院士一生回顧 |author1=Lo, Tung-Bin|author2=Chen, Yung-fa|authorlink2=Chen Yung-fa|author3= Sun, Huimin|author4=Shen, Huaiyu|author5= Chen, Yida|author6=Zhang, Chengwei |isbn=9789860478907 |publisher=Institute of Modern History, Academia Sinica |location=Taipei |year=2016 |oclc=950908333}}</ref> After graduating from [[National Taiwan University]] (NTU), he studied at [[Tohoku University]] in Japan, earning his Ph.D. in chemistry in 1959.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" />

Lo worked as an associate research fellow at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], before returning to Taiwan to join the faculty of NTU. In 1972, on the invitation of [[Chien Shih-Liang]], then president of [[Academia Sinica]], he co-founded the Institute of Biological Chemistry, a joint venture of NTU and Academia Sinica, and served as its first director.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://newsletter.sinica.edu.tw/en/academician-tung-bin-lo-has-passed-away/|title=Academician Tung-bin Lo Has Passed Away|date=2019-05-23|publisher=Academia Sinica|access-date=2019-05-27}}</ref> Lo's teaching career teaching career at NTU spanned from 1964 to 1995.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tung-Bin Lo |url=https://academicians.sinica.edu.tw/index.php?r=academician-n%2Fshow&id=89 |accessdate=19 July 2020 |agency=Academia Sinica}}</ref>

A pioneer in the research on proteins in Taiwan, Lo was elected an academician of Academia Sinica in 1986.<ref name=":2" /> From 1978 to 1990 he served as Dean of the College of Sciences and then Dean of Academic Affairs at NTU.<ref name=":0" /> From 1993 to 1996, he served as Vice President of Academia Sinica.<ref name=":2" /> In January 2016, his memoir was published by the Institute of Modern History of Academia Sinica.<ref name=":1" />

Lo died on 13 May 2019 in Taipei, at the age of 92.<ref name=":2" />
